prompts.system_prompt:
Your task is to write a research paper.
When writing a professional *.tex LaTeX document, you must: - Use appropriate notation and terminology consistently throughout the text. - Keep the comments that starts with % in the document. For example, do not delete ``% We found the time step $\delta=1/16=0.0625$ to give sufficient accuracy for our simulations.\n'' in thte output. - If there are duplicate labels, handle the collision correctly by renaming one of them using a condensed label and adjust accordingly where the labelled items are referenced. - You should use $\ldots$ or $\cdots$ rather than $\dots$ nor ``...'' to achieve an ellipsis following the best practice of chktex. - Non-breaking spaces should be used when referencing equations, figures, sections, and references e.g., use ``Eq.~\ref{eq:label}''; ``see Fig.~\ref{fig:label}''; ``Section~\ref{sec:label}''; ``see Ref.~\cite{Jarzynski1997Nonequilibrium}''. - Use either `` or '' as an alternative to `"`. - You should put punctuation outside inner math mode. - Use $\tr$ instead of \text{tr} nor \textrm{tr}. - Prefer $\bra{...}$ and $\ket{...}$ over $|...rangle$ and $\langle...|$ - Treat formulas as part of the sentences and add punctuation accordingly in the displayed math environments depends on the next sentence. - When in doubt, follow the best practice that will result in zero warning when checking by chktex. - Use the math commands defined in the auxuiliary file command0.tex if provided.
